title: Coding-agent harnesses adopt default-deny toolset gating as standard by H1 2027
body: Nous Research's Blank Slate mode for the open-source Hermes Agent framework, shipped June 20, boots an agent with only a provider/model plus File-Operations and Terminal toolsets, leaving web, browser, code execution, vision, memory, delegation, cron, skills, plugins and MCP servers off until explicitly enabled, and persists those choices durably so a framework update cannot silently re-enable them. That is a textbook least-privilege, attack-surface-reduction posture, and it lands the same week that Codex Record & Replay and Cisco's pipeline-aware FAPO optimizer push more autonomy into the same harnesses. The prediction is that default-off, explicitly-gated toolsets stop being one vendor's opt-in setting and become an expected default for autonomous coding agents: by the first half of 2027 at least three additional named coding-agent harnesses or platforms will ship a least-privilege or default-deny toolset configuration out of the box, or a published agent-security guideline will recommend it as the baseline. The driver is not feature competition but the security reality that an autonomous agent wired to browser, code-exec, MCP and shell access by default is a large, mostly-unaudited attack surface, and durable per-tool gating is the cheapest mitigation that does not break existing workflows.

reasoning.because: Hermes Blank Slate boots File-Ops + Terminal only, all other toolsets default-off and durably pinned
reasoning.given: agents wired to browser/code-exec/MCP/shell by default are a large unaudited attack surface
reasoning.so_that: least-privilege toolset gating becomes the cheapest mitigation that does not break existing agent workflows
reasoning.landing: By H1 2027, 3+ more coding-agent harnesses ship default-deny toolset gating
reasoning.plain_language: Soon most coding robots will start with almost no powers turned on, so a hacked one can do far less damage.

summary: Nous Research's June 20 Hermes Blank Slate mode boots an agent with only file and terminal tools, every other capability off and durably pinned. Answering an attack-surface concern, by H1 2027 three-plus more coding-agent harnesses should ship default-deny toolset gating as baseline.
